summary: As long as we may eat chametz, we may also feed it to animals or sell it. After that time, we may not use it at all. Rabbi Yehuda and the Sages argue how to get rid of it.

chunks.en: The whole time that we may eat chametz,
chunks.st: For the entire time that it is permitted to eat leavened bread,

chunks.en: we may feed it to animals, wild animals and birds,
chunks.st: one may also feed it to his domesticated animals, to non-domesticated animals, and to birds;

chunks.en: and sell it to a non-Jew,
chunks.st: and one may sell it to a gentile;

chunks.en: and we may get use from it.
chunks.st: and it is permitted to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: Once its time has passed,
chunks.st: After its time passes,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from it,
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from it,

chunks.en: and he may not even light an oven or a stove with it.
chunks.st: and one may not even light an oven or a stove with leavened bread.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: With regard to the manner of removal of leavened bread, Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: the only way to get rid of chametz is by burning it.
chunks.st: The removal of leavened bread is to be accomplished only through burning.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he may also crumble it and throw it into the wind,
chunks.st: Burning is not required, as one may even crumble it and throw it into the wind

chunks.en: or throw it into the sea.
chunks.st: or cast it into the sea.

summary: Chametz that belonged to a non-Jew during Pesach may be used after Pesach, but chametz that belonged to a Jew during Pesach may not.

chunks.he: חָמֵץ שֶׁל נָכְרִי שֶׁעָבַר עָלָיו הַפֶּסַח,
chunks.en: Chametz of a non-Jew that was kept over Pesach
chunks.st: It is permitted for a Jew to derive benefit from leavened bread of a gentile

chunks.en: may be used after Pesach.
chunks.st: over which Passover has elapsed,
chunks.stMore: i.e., leavened bread that remains after the conclusion of Passover.

chunks.en: But chametz of a Jew
chunks.st: However, it is prohibited to derive benefit from leaven of a Jew

chunks.en: may not be used,
chunks.st: over which Passover has elapsed,

chunks.en: because it says: It shall not
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And no leavened bread shall be seen with you,

chunks.en: be seen with you, any leaven.
chunks.st: neither shall there be leaven seen with you, in all your borders” (Exodus 13:7).

summary: If a Jew gave chametz to a non-Jew as a pledge for a loan, or the other way around, this mishnah teaches if the chametz may be used after Pesach. It also teaches about chametz that got buried under fallen rocks.

chunks.he: נָכְרִי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ,
chunks.en: A non-Jew who lent money to a Jew, with the Jew's chametz as a pledge:
chunks.explain: The Jew gave his chametz to the non-Jew to hold until he paid back.
chunks.st: If a gentile lent money to a Jew, and the Jew gave him leavened bread as collateral until after Passover,

chunks.en: after Pesach it may be used.
chunks.st: and after Passover the gentile retains this leavened bread in lieu of payment, then one is permitted to derive benefit from this leavened bread.
chunks.stMore: Since the leavened bread was retained by the gentile based on the transfer that took place prior to Passover, the leavened bread is considered to have belonged to the gentile during Passover.

chunks.he: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת הַנָּכְרִי עַל חֲמֵצוֹ,
chunks.en: And a Jew who lent money to a non-Jew, with the non-Jew's chametz as a pledge:
chunks.st: Whereas if a Jew lent money to a gentile, and leavened bread was given as collateral during Passover in the same manner as in the previous case, then

chunks.en: after Pesach it may not be used.
chunks.st: after Passover it is forbidden to derive benefit from this leavened bread.
chunks.stMore: Since this leavened bread was considered to be in the Jew’s property during Passover, it is forbidden to derive benefit from it afterward.

chunks.en: Chametz that a pile of rocks fell on
chunks.st: Leavened bread upon which a rockslide has fallen

chunks.en: counts as if it was gotten rid of.
chunks.st: is considered as though it has been eliminated, and it is not necessary to dig it up in order to burn it.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁאֵין הַכֶּלֶב יָכוֹל לְחַפֵּשׂ אַחֲרָיו:
chunks.en: it must be covered so deep that a dog can't dig for it.
chunks.st: Any leavened bread that has been covered to such an extent that a dog cannot search after it is considered to have been eliminated.

summary: Someone who eats terumah that is chametz on Pesach by mistake must pay the Kohen back. If he did it on purpose, he does not pay.

chunks.en: Someone who eats terumah that is chametz on Pesach by mistake
chunks.st: If one unwittingly eats teruma of leavened bread on Passover, not realizing that the food was teruma, then

chunks.en: pays the main amount plus a fifth more.
chunks.explain: This is what someone pays for eating terumah by mistake.
chunks.st: he must pay the principal and an additional fifth.
chunks.stMore: This is because one who unwittingly eats teruma must compensate the priest for the value of the teruma and add a fifth of the value, even though the teruma is considered to be valueless on Passover. If he

words.note: One fifth more than the main amount.

chunks.en: If on purpose, he does not have to pay, not even its worth as firewood.
chunks.explain: He gets a harsher punishment instead, and chametz on Pesach is worth nothing.
chunks.st: intentionally ate the teruma then he is exempt from payment; as he is liable to receive the severe punishment of karet, he is therefore exempt from the lesser punishment of payment. If he ate impure teruma in this manner then he is not even required to pay its monetary value in wood, for one who derives benefit from impure teruma calculates its value by treating it as though it were fuel for burning. While impure teruma can be used in this manner during the rest of the year, one may not derive any benefit from leavened bread on Passover, and therefore such teruma is worthless.

summary: This mishnah lists the five grains we may use for matzah on Pesach, and which kinds of matzah work for the mitzvah and which do not.

chunks.en: These are the things that a person fulfills
chunks.st: These are the types of grain

chunks.en: his duty with on Pesach:
chunks.st: with which a person fulfills his obligation to eat matza on the first night of Passover:

chunks.en: wheat and barley,
chunks.st: With wheat, with barley,

chunks.en: spelt, rye and oats.
chunks.st: with spelt [kusmin], with rye [shifon], and with oats [shibbolet shu’al].

words.note: Shibboles shual means fox-ear; it is the name of a grain like oats.

chunks.he: וְיוֹצְאִין בִּדְמַאי וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ,
chunks.en: And one fulfills it with demai, and with maaser rishon that had its terumah taken,
chunks.st: And one fulfills his obligation by eating not only matza made from properly tithed grains, but even with matza made from doubtfully tithed produce, and matza made with first tithe from which its teruma was already taken, or

words.note: Food we are not sure had maaser taken from it.
The first tenth, given to the Leviim.

chunks.en: and with maaser sheni and hekdesh that were redeemed.
chunks.st: second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed.

words.note: A tenth that is eaten in Yerushalayim, or redeemed with money.
Things that belong to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: And the Kohanim, with challah and terumah.
chunks.st: And priests may eat matza prepared from ḥalla, the portion of dough that is given to priests, or with teruma, as priests are permitted to eat these portions.

words.note: A piece of dough given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: But not with tevel,
chunks.st: However, one may not fulfill one’s obligation to eat matza made with untithed produce,

words.note: Food that terumah and maaser were not yet taken from.

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ,
chunks.en: and not with maaser rishon that did not have its terumah taken,
chunks.st: nor with matza made from the first tithe from which its teruma was not separated,

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ.
chunks.en: and not with maaser sheni and hekdesh that were not redeemed.
chunks.st: nor with matza made either from the second tithe, nor from consecrated grain that was not redeemed.

chunks.en: Loaves of a korban todah and wafers of a nazir:
chunks.st: With regard to one who prepared loaves of matza that are brought with a thanks-offering, or to the wafers brought by a nazirite, the Sages drew the following distinction:

words.note: Someone who promised not to drink wine or cut his hair for a while.

chunks.en: if he made them for himself,
chunks.st: If he prepared them for himself, then he

chunks.en: we don't fulfill the mitzvah with them.
chunks.st: does not fulfill his obligation to eat matza with them.

chunks.en: If he made them to sell in the market,
chunks.st: However, if he prepared them to sell them in the market to those who require these loaves or wafers,

chunks.en: we do fulfill the mitzvah with them.
chunks.st: one fulfills the obligation to eat matza with them.

summary: This mishnah lists the vegetables we may use for maror at the Seder, and how they may be prepared.

chunks.en: And these are the vegetables that a person fulfills
chunks.st: And these are the vegetables with which a person can

chunks.en: his duty with on Pesach:
chunks.st: fulfill his obligation to eat bitter herbs on Passover:

chunks.en: romaine lettuce, endives, horseradish, eryngo and maror.
chunks.st: One can fulfill his obligation with ḥazeret, with chervil [tamkha], and with field eryngo [ḥarḥavina], and with endives [olashin], and with maror.

words.note: Steinsaltz says chervil; many say horseradish.

chunks.he: יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בֵּין לַחִין בֵּין יְבֵשִׁין,
chunks.en: We fulfill it with them whether fresh or dry,
chunks.st: One fulfills his obligation with them whether they are fresh or whether they are dry.

chunks.en: but not pickled, and not
chunks.st: However, one does not fulfill his obligation if they are pickled in water or vinegar, nor if they are

chunks.en: boiled too long, and not cooked.
chunks.st: over-boiled [shaluk] in hot water, nor if they are boiled [mevushal].

chunks.en: And they join together to make a kezayis.
chunks.st: The mishna adds: And all these different types of vegetables join together to the measure of an olive-bulk,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it is not necessary to eat this amount from one specific type of vegetable.

words.note: A kezayis, the amount we must eat.

chunks.en: And we fulfill it with their stalk,
chunks.st: And one fulfills his obligation by eating their stalk,
chunks.stMore: as it is not necessary to eat the leaves. And one fulfills the obligation

chunks.en: and with demai, and with maaser rishon that had its terumah taken,
chunks.st: with doubtfully tithed produce, with first-tithe produce whose teruma has been taken and given to a priest, and with both

chunks.en: and with maaser sheni and hekdesh that were redeemed.
chunks.st: second-tithe produce and consecrated property that were redeemed.

summary: On Pesach we may not soak bran or wheat in water, because it might become chametz.

chunks.en: We may not soak bran for chickens,
chunks.st: One may not soak coarse bran for feeding chickens, lest it be leavened.

words.note: The rough outside part of the grain.

chunks.en: but we may pour boiling water on it.
chunks.st: However, one may pour boiling water onto the bran before feeding it to the chickens,
chunks.stMore: as it will not become leavened from this brief exposure to water.

chunks.en: A woman may not soak
chunks.st: A woman may not soak coarse bran to

chunks.en: the bran that she carries in her hand to the bathhouse,
chunks.st: bring by hand to the bathhouse for use as a cleanser;

chunks.en: but she may rub it dry on her skin.
chunks.st: however, she may rub coarse bran on her dry skin.

chunks.en: A person may not chew wheat
chunks.st: Likewise, the Sages said: A person may not chew wheat

chunks.en: and put it on his wound on Pesach,
chunks.st: and place it on his wound,

chunks.en: because it becomes chametz.
chunks.st: due to the fact that the wheat will be leavened from the saliva and his chewing.

summary: This mishnah teaches about putting flour into charoses or mustard, how the korban Pesach may not be cooked, and water a baker used.

chunks.en: We may not put flour into
chunks.st: One may not add flour to

chunks.en: the charoses or into the mustard.
chunks.st: ḥaroset, a seasoned, pungent food, or to mustard, to dull the sharp taste.
chunks.stMore: In both cases, the pungency of these foods might accelerate the leavening of the flour.

words.note: A sharp-tasting food made from fruit and spices.

chunks.en: And if he put it in,
chunks.st: And if one added flour to either of these, the mixture may

chunks.en: it should be eaten right away.
chunks.st: be eaten immediately before it is leavened;

chunks.en: And Rabbi Meir forbids it.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Meir prohibits this, lest the food be leavened immediately.

chunks.en: We may not cook the korban Pesach, not
chunks.st: The mishna continues: One may not boil the Paschal lamb

words.note: The korban Pesach, the Pesach lamb.

chunks.en: in liquids and not in fruit juices.
chunks.explain: The Torah says it must be roasted.
chunks.st: in ordinary liquids or in fruit juices, as the Torah explicitly states that it must be roasted.

chunks.en: But we may baste it and dip it in them.
chunks.st: However, one may baste it while it is roasting and dip it into liquid while eating it.

chunks.en: The water a baker used
chunks.st: The tanna further states: Water that has been used by a baker for cooling his hands or washing dishes should

chunks.en: must be poured out, because it makes things chametz.
chunks.st: be poured out, because this water leavens the dough, as the water probably contains a small quantity of flour and dough.
